problem: Overexpansion and brand dilution had drained cash.
title: Lego sells non-core assets and refocuses on its core toy business
context: Lego had expanded into theme parks, video games and clothing and was close to bankruptcy in 2004.
decision_made: Sell peripheral businesses including control of the Legoland parks, cut costs and refocus on core products.
action_taken: New CEO Jorgen Vig Knudstorp sold a 70 percent stake in the parks for $460 million to Blackstone and cut jobs.
observed_outcome: Lego was profitable again by 2006, and by 2014 it passed Mattel as the world's largest toy company by revenue and profit.
lessons: Focusing on a core business and selling assets can rescue an overextended company.
limitations: Debt and job-cut figures differ across sources. Some figures come from blog posts and business summaries.

claims.claim_text: Lego sold a 70 percent stake in its Legoland parks for $460 million and refocused on core products.
Britannica credits the CEO with turning Lego around and reports it became the largest toy maker by 2014.
